text:
Situation: Sucralfate 1 g tablets have been on FDA's shortage list since 2023-01-04 and remained listed as of 2026-10-21, a duration of 46 months. Corvale East holds 126 tablets (16.6 days on hand at 7.6 tablets per day). Corvale General holds 193 tablets (18.9 days on hand at 10.2 tablets per day).

Why (FDA record): FDA's shortage list shows sucralfate posted 2023-01-04 and still listed 2026-10-21. The product label for NDC 67296214704 identifies Redpharm Drug as labeler and plant (FEI 3003719240) with operations listed as REPACK. FDA inspection 1277212 at that plant ended 2025-08-01 and was classified VAI, classification known 2025-10-22. An earlier inspection 1030658 at the same plant ended 2017-11-03 and was also classified VAI, known 2018-02-01.

Our position: Current inventory covers less than three weeks at both sites. The rule-based best option is to buy from Allergan, Inc., which is not on FDA's shortage list today and uses plant ABBVIE.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to place orders with Allergan, Inc. for sucralfate 1 g tablets; requires P&T committee approval.
2. Buyer to qualify Amneal Pharmaceuticals NY LLC as secondary source (plant last inspection NAI 2023-06-07); requires P&T committee approval.
3. Buyer to qualify Teva Pharmaceuticals USA, Inc. as tertiary source; requires P&T committee approval.
4. Buyer to evaluate Advanced Rx Pharmacy of Tennessee, LLC and Advanced Rx of Tennessee, LLC if primary and secondary sources cannot supply; requires P&T committee approval.

Not recommended: Continuing to rely on Redpharm Drug supply given the prolonged shortage listing and VAI inspection history at its plant.
